items.title: E1. Common-shift invariance
items.prompt: Hold q, k, and the frequencies fixed. Prove that shifting both positions by $c$ leaves a RoPE dot product unchanged.
items.answer:
*Solution.*

$$
(R_{m+c}q)^T(R_{n+c}k)
=q^TR_{m+c}^TR_{n+c}k
=q^TR_{n-m}k.
$$

This uses $R_a^T=R_{-a}$ and the rotation group law $R_aR_b=R_{a+b}$. Thus $R_{m+c}^TR_{n+c}=R_{-(m+c)}R_{n+c}=R_{n-m}$. The shared offset cancels: with q and k fixed, position enters only through relative displacement $n-m$.

items.title: E2. Spectral coverage
items.prompt: For $D=64$, count the pairs completing at least one turn by position 4096 for bases 10,000, 150,000, and 500,000.
items.answer:
*Solution.* Rotary pair $i=0,\ldots,D/2-1$ has frequency $\theta_i=\text{base}^{-2i/D}$. It completes a turn when $L\theta_i\ge2\pi$, or

$$
i\le \frac{D}{2}\frac{\ln(L/2\pi)}{\ln(\text{base})}.
$$

For $D=64$ and $L=4096$, the right-hand side is about 22.52, 17.40, and 15.80. Counting integer indices from zero gives **23, 18, and 16** pairs. This is phase coverage in the chosen window, not a hard count of distinguishable positions.

items.title: E3. YaRN scenario
items.prompt: With base 150,000, factor 32, $D=64$, reference length 4096, $\beta_{fast}=32$, and $\beta_{slow}=1$, compute the ramp and scaling factors.
items.answer:
*Solution.* Substitution into the original gpt-oss ramp-boundary formulas gives `low≈8.0928` and `high≈17.3980`. Hence pairs $i=0,\ldots,8$ retain their original frequencies (9 pairs), $i=9,\ldots,17$ are transitional (9), and $i=18,\ldots,31$ are fully interpolated (14). With `truncate=True`, the stored boundaries are `8/18`, while the integer partition remains the same.

The attention factor is $a=1+0.1\ln32=1.346574$. If both $q$ and $k$ receive it, bilinearity gives $(aq)^T(ak)=a^2q^Tk$, so the score factor is $a^2=1.813260$, not $a$.

items.title: E4. Text M-RoPE
items.prompt: Show that coordinates $(m,m,m)$ produce the same output as standard 1D RoPE.
items.answer: *Solution.* M-RoPE assigns rotary pairs to axes such as time, height, and width. A text token uses coordinates $(m,m,m)$, so every pair with frequency $\theta_i$ receives angle $m\theta_i$, regardless of its axis assignment. Concatenating all pairs therefore reproduces standard 1D RoPE exactly. A difference appears only when a multimodal token has unequal axis coordinates.
